strategy.thesis: Single-family office of the Tsao family that pursues both impact-focused and ESG-aware investments across public and private markets, with health explicitly named as one of its core impact themes; investment returns are directed to fund the family's Tsao Foundation and Tsao Family Foundation, which are active in eldercare and community health in Singapore, giving the office a direct biomedical/health-philanthropy nexus.

summary.en: Singapore single-family office investing across asset classes with an explicit impact mandate in climate, health and education; profits fund the healthcare/eldercare-focused Tsao Foundation.

sources.title: Tsao Family Office
sources.supports: Impact investment focus including health; funds Tsao Foundation
sources.quote: There is certain impact themes that are of particular interest to the TFO that include, but are not limited to: climate/environment, health and education. ... The TFO's financial objectives are to earn a sufficient return to fund the various philanthropic activities of the family (via the Tsao Foundation and Tsao Family Foundation.)

sources.title: The Single-Family Office as Champion and Catalyst for Impact & ESG-Centric Investing
sources.quote: Founded in 2016, Tsao Family Office manages the Tsao family's global assets with a strong emphasis on sustainability and values-based investing, investing in global equities, fixed income, and private markets, focusing on sectors such as climate, health, and education.

verification_notes: Health is one of several named impact themes (alongside climate/environment and education), not the office's exclusive focus; included because the health/eldercare nexus via Tsao Foundation is explicit and verifiable on the official site.

strategy.thesis: Singapore-based multi-family office and investment ecosystem (Golden Equator Wealth / Capital) whose SPECTRUM business club launched a dedicated Korea-Singapore Healthcare Incubator in partnership with Korean healthcare investor C&R Healthcare Global, helping 10-15 Korean medical-device, medtech and cosmeceutical companies expand into Southeast Asia — the group's clearest biomedical nexus alongside its broader wealth-management and venture activity.

perks: access to investors and business partners

summary.en: Singapore multi-family office whose SPECTRUM ecosystem operates the Korea-Singapore Healthcare Incubator, supporting Korean medtech and healthcare companies entering Southeast Asia.

sources.title: Golden Equator Group Ecosystem
sources.supports: Multi-family office structure with SPECTRUM ecosystem
sources.quote: Golden Equator Wealth is a Singapore-based multi-family office specialising in private wealth management and succession planning.

sources.title: Singapore: Golden Equator-C&R Healthcare Global partner to launch incubator
sources.supports: Korea-Singapore Healthcare Incubator launch and healthcare/medtech focus
sources.quote: SPECTRUM is home to the "Korea-Singapore Healthcare Incubator" which was established in September 2017 through an MOU between Golden Equator Group and a Korean entity C&R Healthcare, appointed by the City of Seoul BioHub and Korean Health Industry Development Institution (KHIDI). The Incubator helps 10-15 Korean health companies expand into Singapore and Southeast Asia.

verification_notes: Healthcare incubator (SPECTRUM / Korea-Singapore Healthcare Incubator) was launched in 2017 via press coverage (DealStreetAsia, e27); could not confirm from a fetched primary source whether the program is still actively running today, so treat the health-specific activity as historically verified rather than confirmed-current.

name.en: AVPN Southeast Asia Healthcare Pooled Fund

strategy.thesis: First-of-its-kind pooled philanthropic fund in Southeast Asia, administered by AVPN (Asian Venture Philanthropy Network) and capitalised by funders including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Johnson & Johnson, Sequoia, Macquarie, Chevron and the Vitol Foundation, deploying unrestricted grant capital to nonprofits that strengthen primary healthcare access in rural/underserved areas and support pandemic resilience in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.

summary.en: AVPN-administered pooled philanthropic fund that channels catalytic grant capital from major funders (Gates Foundation, J&J, Sequoia, Macquarie, Chevron) into primary healthcare and pandemic-resilience nonprofits across Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines.

sources.title: AVPN Southeast Asia Healthcare Pooled Fund
sources.supports: Fund structure, backers, focus countries, health focus, grant size, first-round grantees
sources.quote: The first of its kind in Southeast Asia, the AVPN Philanthropic Pooled Fund is focused on supporting healthcare systems in rural and hard-to-reach urban areas in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Philippines. ... received 85 strong applications with a collective ask of USD 40 million ... Multiple major organizations fund the initiative, including the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Johnson & Johnson, Sequoia, Macquarie, Chevron, and the Vitol Foundation ... Organizations can request between USD 100,000 and USD 300,000 in unrestricted funding. The first funding round (2021-2022) awarded grants to four nonprofits: ASSIST, CISDI, IIRR, and IRC.

verification_notes: Fund is administered by AVPN (headquartered in Singapore) but deploys entirely into Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines; listed under Singapore as the administering HQ per scope instructions. Could not confirm whether further funding rounds occurred after 2021-2022.

strategy.thesis: Family philanthropic foundation of Sukanto and Tinah Tanoto (founders of RGE) that has provided catalytic funding for scalable healthcare and medical-research initiatives since 2009 — including endowed professorships and research initiatives in diabetes, medical oncology and cardiovascular medicine at SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre — and that actively promotes the venture-philanthropy model of patient, catalytic capital through AVPN.

summary.en: Indonesian family foundation of the Tanoto family (RGE) that funds scalable healthcare and medical-research programs, including diabetes/oncology/cardiovascular professorships at SingHealth Duke-NUS and Indonesia's Ministry of Health digital primary-care transformation.

sources.title: Tanoto Foundation
sources.supports: Foundation founding, health/medical research funding, SingHealth Duke-NUS partnership
sources.quote: Since 2009, Tanoto Foundation has contributed catalytic funding to support scalable healthcare and medical research initiatives. Tanoto Foundation partners with SingHealth Duke-NUS Academic Medical Centre to establish Professorships and Research Initiatives in the areas of Diabetes, Medical Oncology and Cardiovascular Medicine.

sources.title: Tanoto Foundation Highlights Need to Catalyse Funding to Address Social Challenges
sources.supports: Venture-philanthropy framing; Global Fund TB/HIV/malaria contribution; Indonesia Ministry of Health digital health partnership
sources.quote: The world needs more of this type of capital – flexible, patient, long term, early stage capital, which is best provided by foundations and philanthropy organizations.

verification_notes: Health is one of several foundation pillars (alongside education, which is the larger historical focus); founding year 1981 refers to the family's original philanthropic activity, formal foundation incorporation was 2001. Facts drawn from the foundation's own site via search snippets rather than a full page fetch.

strategy.thesis: Philippine family foundation established by the Zuellig family (now operationally separate from the Zuellig pharmaceutical-distribution group) that funds and builds local-government health-leadership and governance capacity to improve maternal, child and adolescent health outcomes in underserved municipalities.

summary.en: Manila-based family foundation of the Zuellig family that funds health-leadership and governance programs to improve maternal, newborn and adolescent health outcomes in underserved Philippine municipalities.

sources.title: Zuellig Family Foundation
sources.supports: Founding year, mission, separation from Zuellig Group, focus areas
sources.quote: The foundation was established in 1997 as the Pharmaceutical Health and Family Foundation and was renamed to Zuellig Family Foundation in 2008. ZFF became separate and distinct from the Zuellig Group of Companies and its affiliates, and operates as a registered non-profit family foundation in the Philippines.

sources.title: Who We Are
sources.quote: In their current 2022-2031 strategy, ZFF continues to build local government capacity through key work areas in Local Health Systems, Nutrition Governance, and Adolescent and Youth Sexual Reproductive Health (AYSRH).

verification_notes: Operates as a grant-making health-governance foundation rather than a direct equity/venture investor in health startups; included under the disease-foundation / venture-philanthropy type per scope. 'Founded_year' 1997 is under its original name (Pharmaceutical Health and Family Foundation); renamed 2008.
